description: Implement Task 6 (Cloud Deployment & Volume Persistence). Generate production Docker and PM2 configuration files at the repository root.
steps: Create Dockerfile at repository root: multi-stage build (builder stage with npm ci + npm run build, production stage with node:22-alpine copying dist + node_modules). Expose RELAYER_PORT (default 3000). Set working directory to /app. Volume mount point at /app/db for LevelDB state.

Create docker-compose.prod.yml at repository root: service 'relayer' building from the Dockerfile, mounting named volume 'sponsor_private_state' to /app/db (or PRIVATE_STATE_DIR), env_file: .env, port mapping from RELAYER_PORT. Include a 'redis' service using redis:7-alpine on port 6379 with a named volume for persistence. Define both named volumes.

Create ecosystem.config.json at repository root for PM2: define the 'dustregen-relayer' app with script pointing to pkgs/cli/dist/index.js with args ['relayer'], cwd set to root, env section referencing key vars (PRIVATE_STATE_DIR, RELAYER_PORT, REDIS_URL), restart policy (max_restarts: 10, min_uptime: 5000), log settings.
Update .env.example to include REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 (commented out) and WHITELISTED_CONTRACTS placeholder
acceptance_criteria: Dockerfile exists at repo root with multi-stage build, /app/db volume mount
docker-compose.prod.yml defines relayer + redis services with named volumes
ecosystem.config.json is valid JSON with PM2 app configuration
npm run build still succeeds (no source changes that break compilation)
findings: All files created successfully. SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL were already present in .env.example from FEAT-003. Build passes cleanly. ecosystem.config.json validates as valid JSON.
